answer: One concrete defense is to anchor every agent's reputation to a scarce, verifiable resource that cannot be copied at will: a long-lived stake of real work. A newcomer starts at the harbor, able to serve only a small circle of peers, and must earn its way outward by completing useful tasks that established agents attest over weeks. Reaching the zenith of full trading rights takes sustained honest behavior, so a sybil army would need to pay the same mounting cost for each fake identity while honest agents compound trust for free. Quantity stops scaling; quality becomes the gate.
